literal: Before stronger people oneself let one think, when oneself against those weaker than oneself goes.
translation: When a person goes to oppress those who are weaker than themselves, let them think of how they would stand helpless before those who are stronger than themselves.
modern: ஒருவர் தன்னை விட மெலிந்தவர் மேல் துன்பம் செய்யச் செல்லும்போது, தன்னை விட வலியவர் முன்னால் தான் அஞ்சி நிற்கும் நிலையை நினைக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet teaches empathy and compassion by appealing to our own sense of vulnerability. When we are in a position of power, we often forget the pain of the weak and act ruthlessly. The poet advises that before we oppress someone weaker ('மெலியார்'), we should imagine ourselves standing helpless before someone stronger ('வலியார்') than us. This mental shift evokes the feeling of fear and vulnerability, which immediately curbs our desire to harm the weak, fostering compassion ('அருள்').
